recommendation.text: There were no voting questions. After discussing concerns about antimicrobial cross-resistance and inappropriate empiric ambulatory use, the committee recommended restricting the indication and adding limitations of use.

quote.quote: Given the totality of evidence presented in the FDA Briefing Document and the concerns outlined above, the AC members recommended restricting the indication and providing limitations of use statements.

linkages.concern: AMDAC members raised concern that unrestricted empiric use of an oral penem for uUTI in the ambulatory setting could drive antimicrobial cross-resistance to carbapenems, harming both individual patients and society.
linkages.change: The Indication was narrowed to restrict use to adult women who have limited or no alternative oral antibacterial treatment options.

concern_quote.quote: Although there were no voting questions, the AC members discussed concerns for potential downstream risks to both individual patients and to society from antimicrobial cross-resistance to carbapenems arising from unrestricted empiric use of oral sulopenem for uUTI in an ambulatory setting.

change_quote.quote: Indication statement edited to restrict use of sulopenem based on feedback obtained from the 9/9/2024 Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee (AMDAC) panel regarding the most appropriate use of sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid

linkages.concern: The committee recommended providing limitations of use statements to address the risk of off-label use, given the lack of demonstrated efficacy outside uUTI.
linkages.change: Limitations of Use were added stating ORLYNVAH is not indicated for cUTI or cIAI or as step-down treatment after IV antibacterial treatment of cUTI/cIAI, to mitigate off-label use.

summary: Because oral sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid would be the first oral penem on the U.S. market, FDA convened the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee on September 9, 2024. There were no voting questions; committee members raised concerns about antimicrobial cross-resistance and inappropriate empiric ambulatory use and recommended restricting the indication and adding limitations of use. The review team, citing this feedback, narrowed the indication to women with limited or no alternative oral options, added cUTI/cIAI limitations of use, and reworded the labeling 'Usage' heading to emphasize reducing drug-resistant bacteria.
